title: Velocity, Docks, Type & Windows
description: Five patterns that read the speed and direction of input, not just its position — a hysteresis reading mode, a pinnable dock, velocity type, a spinning cursor badge, and a real window manager.

drops.title: Skim Reader
drops.description: A scroll-velocity hysteresis state machine that instantly collapses content into skim mode, then waits out a dead zone before trusting you're reading again.
drops.concept: Enters skim mode the instant smoothed scroll velocity crosses a high threshold, but only exits back to detailed mode after velocity stays under a lower threshold continuously for a hold time — the asymmetric gap between the two thresholds is what kills flicker from noisy scroll signals.

interaction.mouse: Scroll fast to trigger skim mode, slow down and hold to return to detailed mode
interaction.click: Tune enter/exit thresholds and dead time, or use the Simulate Fast Flick button
interaction.touch: Fast swipe-scroll triggers the same hysteresis logic

drops.title: Command Dock
drops.description: A start/center/end command dock you populate by dragging icons out of a library — toggles fire inline, palettes expand straight out of the icon.
drops.concept: Reimplements the region-based pinnable dock from Windows' Command Palette: three flex regions hold draggable command chips persisted to localStorage. Toggle-type commands run immediately in place; palette-type commands do a shared-element (FLIP) expand from the chip's own bounding rect into a centered overlay.

interaction.mouse: Drag chips between the library and dock regions, click a pinned chip to run it
interaction.click: Toggle commands run inline; palette commands expand into an overlay
interaction.touch: Pointer-Events-based drag works identically on touch

drops.title: Velocity Type
drops.description: Three headlines answer your pointer's speed, not its position, with variable-font weight, slant, 3D tilt and tracking — smoothed so it never jitters.
drops.concept: Tracks signed pointer (or scroll) velocity, smooths it with a tunable exponential moving average, then maps the result to font-variation-settings axes (wght/opsz/slnt), letter-spacing, opacity and a perspective/rotate tilt whose direction follows the velocity's sign. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

interaction.mouse: Move fast or slow to change weight, slant and tilt in real time
interaction.click: Switch velocity source between pointer and scroll, tune smoothing and max tilt
interaction.touch: Falls back gracefully; scroll-velocity mode works on touch

drops.title: Spin Badge Cursor
drops.description: A frame-rate-independent damped cursor that expands into a rotating badge on hover — spin direction flips live with your movement direction.
drops.concept: A custom cursor follower interpolates toward the real pointer position each frame using a damping formula normalized to elapsed time (not frame count), so it looks identical at 30fps or 120fps. Hovering a target scales it into a badge; the badge's continuous rotation direction is set from the sign of the pointer's horizontal movement.

interaction.mouse: Move around, hover a card to see the badge expand and spin
interaction.touch: Custom cursor is disabled; cards get a tap-scale response instead

drops.title: Window Engine
drops.description: A tiny in-browser desktop: draggable, titled, stackable windows launched from a dock, with focus-raise, minimize and close — a real window manager, not another modal.
drops.concept: Each app spawns a floating window with a colored, draggable title bar; clicking anywhere on a window raises its z-index to bring it to front. Minimize tucks it into a pill dock; close removes it entirely. Notes persist to localStorage and a tiny terminal responds to a few real commands.
tech: Pointer Events drag + z-index focus stack

interaction.mouse: Drag windows by their title bar, click to focus, use the — and ✕ buttons
interaction.click: Dock icons open or focus an app's window
interaction.touch: Dragging and tapping both work via Pointer Events
